# injecta

> Compile-time dependency injection for Rust. You declare a container once with `container!`, derive `Injectable` on your types, and call `resolve`. Every dependency is checked by the compiler: a missing provider, a dependency cycle or a singleton that depends on a request-scoped value does not compile. There is no runtime registry, no `TypeId` map, no locks and no `dyn` on the resolve path: a resolve compiles to constructor calls and `Arc` clones, within about 1 ns of hand-written wiring on the comparison benchmark.

Generated from GUIDE.md by `just docs`; do not edit.
